A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Colonial conflict, migrations, distinct communities and later descendant histories. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] si.edu

Sources for map connections

  • South Carolina · Historical towns / settlement connection

    DePratter documents Yamasee towns around St. Helena, Port Royal Sound and the Ashepoo/Combahee rivers in South Carolina. Inspection: Form authorship; historic context E pp. 3–6; geographical data G p. 1. Limits: Historical settlement association; changing composite identity acknowledged, with no present recognition or boundary claim.

    • Yamasee Indian Towns in the South Carolina Lowcountry, 1684–1715
    • Supporting source from nps.gov

  • Florida · Historical refuge / migration connection

    The account describes Yamasee near St. Augustine before migration to Carolina and refuge with Spanish St. Augustine after the war. Inspection: Historic context E pp. 3 and 6. Limits: Historical Florida connection; not exclusive homeland or present government location.

    • Yamasee Indian Towns in the South Carolina Lowcountry, 1684–1715

  • Georgia · Historical coastal community connection

    John E. Worth describes Yamasee groups settling briefly among the Mocama and Guale during the Georgia mission era. National Park Service interpretation describes the group in historical regional context.

    • Spanish Missions
    • Supporting source from nps.gov
